FLASHCARD SET · AGES 2 YEARS

Garden Friends flashcards.

Eighteen cards about the animals who live around your house: in the hedge, under the tree, by the pond. Rabbits, hedgehogs, ducks and friends — every one looked at from a kind distance, never grabbed.

These cards belong to School Garden · Age 2 on the Kiddo School learning path.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    Match card to real life

    Keep two or three cards by the window. When a bird lands or a squirrel dashes by, grab the card and match it — the garden becomes part of the deck.

  2. 02

    Move like the animal

    Hop like a rabbit, waddle like a duck, scurry like a squirrel. Toddlers remember animals in their legs before they remember them in words.

  3. 03

    Wild means look-only

    Say the rule gently and often: wild animals stay wild — we watch, we wave, we never grab. It is the kindest thing a two-year-old can learn about animals.

  4. 04

    Two cards per walk

    Pick the rabbit and the bird card, then see which one shows up first. A small deck travels light and keeps the game going all the way round the block.

      FLASHCARD · GARDEN FRIENDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Bird Flashcard for Toddlers

      The garden's most faithful visitor, back every morning whether anyone claps or not. This card turns your window into a hide: seeds on the sill, quiet feet, and a bird that trusts the stillness.

      Teaching tips

      What this card plants

      Gives the morning chorus a familiar face before you have left the house.

      Meet one for real

      Find one on the pavement or lawn and match it to the picture.

      What kids learn from it

      Builds watching habits that turn every walk into a quiet safari.

      How to print it

      Thick card survives a year of window duty.

      Grown-up tip

      Learn the three commonest visitors first — pigeon counts as a win.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Bird lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · GARDEN FRIENDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Frog Flashcard for Toddlers

      The pond-side regular with the long legs and the sudden vanishing act. Frogs sit still so well that spotting one feels earned — then it jumps, and the game starts again.

      Teaching tips

      What this card plants

      Names the pond-side jumper so water visits feel like meeting an old friend.

      Meet one for real

      Visit the pond in spring and crouch low — someone usually peeps back.

      What kids learn from it

      Teaches that wild things are met slowly, from the safe side.

      How to print it

      A wipe-clean sleeve helps — ponds and drizzle go together.

      Grown-up tip

      If it jumps, the delight doubles — stay a while.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Frog lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · GARDEN FRIENDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Squirrel Flashcard for Toddlers

      The park's fastest acrobat, all tail and urgency. Squirrels perform all year — up the tree, down the tree, zigzag along the fence — and toddlers are their most devoted audience.

      Teaching tips

      What this card plants

      Turns the park's show-off into a name your child owns forever.

      Meet one for real

      Try the big trees at the park's edge — tails flash early there.

      What kids learn from it

      Sharpens noticing — a flash of tail, then gone up the trunk.

      How to print it

      Print small for pockets and large for the kitchen wall.

      Grown-up tip

      Let them stare — staring is how children and squirrels take stock.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Squirrel lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · GARDEN FRIENDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Rabbit Flashcard for Toddlers

      The twitchy-nosed hopper every toddler knows from books and breakfast cereal boxes. Rabbits are gentle to look at and fast to leave, which makes the card the most patient rabbit you will ever meet.

      Teaching tips

      What this card plants

      Introduces the twitchy-nosed hopper toddlers already half know from stories.

      Meet one for real

      Meet one at a city farm and count the hops between nibbles.

      What kids learn from it

      Builds gentle admiration for animals that prefer not to be touched.

      How to print it

      Card stock and rounded corners — rabbit cards get loved to bits.

      Grown-up tip

      Hop-talk helps — describe the springy legs while you watch together.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Rabbit lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · GARDEN FRIENDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Hedgehog Flashcard for Toddlers

      The hedgehog — a pincushion with legs, out at night snuffling for slugs. Most toddlers meet hedgehogs in stories first, which is fitting: a storybook animal with a real prickly personality.

      Teaching tips

      What this card plants

      Explains the prickly night wanderer most children meet in books first.

      Meet one for real

      Check the lawn at dusk from the window — hedgehogs keep late hours.

      What kids learn from it

      Practises the no-touch rule with a creature that clearly agrees.

      How to print it

      Print a spare — this one gets asked for at bedtime.

      Grown-up tip

      Spines are protection, not rudeness — say so, twice if needed.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Hedgehog lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · GARDEN FRIENDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Worm Flashcard for Toddlers

      The garden's underground gardener, quietly turning leaves into soil. Worms are the least glamorous card in the set and the most important — no worms, no garden.

      Teaching tips

      What this card plants

      Puts the wiggliest helper in the whole garden onto one card.

      Meet one for real

      After rain, watch one cross the pavement — no fingers needed today.

      What kids learn from it

      Nudges respect for the small, quiet jobs that keep gardens alive.

      How to print it

      Laminate this one — worm weather is wet weather.

      Grown-up tip

      Never poke — the wiggle tells you everything from a step away.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Worm lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · GARDEN FRIENDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Duck Flashcard for Toddlers

      The pond's busiest resident, bottom-up in the water and quacking instructions. Ducks are usually the first wild animal a toddler feeds — or rather, used to feed: these days we watch and quack instead.

      Teaching tips

      What this card plants

      Names the pond's chattiest regular, already famous from bath time.

      Meet one for real

      Park ponds count as appointments — waddle to the bank and say hello.

      What kids learn from it

      Links picture to pond life and builds early water-side sense.

      How to print it

      Card stock for the buggy basket — this card commutes.

      Grown-up tip

      The bank is the meeting spot — keep small feet behind yours.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Duck lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · GARDEN FRIENDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Turtle Flashcard for Toddlers

      The turtle, carrying its house and in no hurry whatsoever. It is the slowest card in the deck and the best teacher of the slow game: everything arrives eventually, especially turtles.

      Teaching tips

      What this card plants

      Explains a creature that carries its house and refuses every hurry.

      Meet one for real

      Meet one at a pond, pet shop window or zoo — slow looking wins.

      What kids learn from it

      Practises patience by example — slow things reward slow watchers.

      How to print it

      Two copies work — the spare survives bath-time commentary.

      Grown-up tip

      Say slow a few beats longer than feels natural.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Turtle lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · GARDEN FRIENDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Mouse Flashcard for Toddlers

      The mouse — small, quick and mostly seen as a dash along the fence. On the card it sits still for once, whiskers and all, which is the only way most toddlers ever get a good look.

      Teaching tips

      What this card plants

      Gives the shy garden dasher a friendly face instead of a scream.

      Meet one for real

      Real ones hide, so try the shed corner at dusk — from a distance.

      What kids learn from it

      Builds comfort with shy things — not everyone wants to say hello.

      How to print it

      Ordinary paper suits a card this small and quick.

      Grown-up tip

      Keep the calm voice going — squeals scatter more than mice.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Mouse lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · GARDEN FRIENDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Mole Flashcard for Toddlers

      The mole — almost blind, brilliant at tunnels, and rarely seen above ground. Most toddlers know moles from the molehills that appear on lawns like little volcanoes overnight.

      Teaching tips

      What this card plants

      Introduces the underground tunneller almost nobody ever actually sees.

      Meet one for real

      Hunt for molehills on park grass — proof somebody is busy below.

      What kids learn from it

      Sparks curiosity about hidden lives and what hills can reveal.

      How to print it

      Card stock, then hole-punch and ring it into a field pack.

      Grown-up tip

      A real molehill is treasure — mark it, check again next week.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Mole lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · GARDEN FRIENDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Lizard Flashcard for Toddlers

      The lizard, sunbathing on a warm rock, perfectly still until — gone. Lizards are the garden's quick-change artists, and their stillness game is worth stealing for toddler purposes.

      Teaching tips

      What this card plants

      Names the sunbathing sprinter of warm rocks and old stone walls.

      Meet one for real

      On warm days, watch sunny rockeries and walls for a sudden scuttle.

      What kids learn from it

      Trains sharp eyes for stillness — spotting one takes proper looking.

      How to print it

      Print bright — lizards vanish into the picture if ink is faint.

      Grown-up tip

      Freeze when you spot one — lizards trust watchers who stop moving.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Lizard lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · GARDEN FRIENDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Toad Flashcard for Toddlers

      The toad — the frog's warty, walk-when-you-could-jump cousin. Toads prefer gardens to ponds and come out on damp evenings, which makes them the after-dark surprise card.

      Teaching tips

      What this card plants

      Gives the warty garden walker its proper billing, no jumping required.

      Meet one for real

      Damp evenings in the veg patch are toad time — look, then tiptoe off.

      What kids learn from it

      Teaches comparing — smooth versus bumpy, jumper versus walker.

      How to print it

      Keep it beside the frog card — the pair does the teaching.

      Grown-up tip

      Never pick one up — warts are for looking at only.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Toad lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · GARDEN FRIENDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Chipmunk Flashcard for Toddlers

      The chipmunk — a squirrel striped for speed, cheeks stuffed with seeds. It is the busiest packer in the garden, and the cheek-pouches are the detail toddlers remember forever.

      Teaching tips

      What this card plants

      Shows the striped speed-gatherer with pockets full of lunch.

      Meet one for real

      Parks and woodland edges are best — listen for scolding from low branches.

      What kids learn from it

      Feeds early ideas about storing, collecting and planning ahead.

      How to print it

      Two copies print well — matching the stripes is half the fun.

      Grown-up tip

      Follow the cheeks — wherever they go, a stash is near.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Chipmunk lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · GARDEN FRIENDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Raccoon Flashcard for Toddlers

      The raccoon with the bandit mask and clever little hands, famous for investigating everything. It is the night crew's most curious member — and its mask makes it instantly recognizable, even in a book.

      Teaching tips

      What this card plants

      Explains the masked night visitor who sorts out our bins overnight.

      Meet one for real

      Bin lids left ajar at dawn are raccoon clues — read them together.

      What kids learn from it

      Grows the bedtime-mystery muscle — masked visitors make excellent stories.

      How to print it

      Sturdy stock for this one — the character needs a stage.

      Grown-up tip

      Real raccoons stay wild — masks belong on cards, not on pets.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Raccoon lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · GARDEN FRIENDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Deer Flashcard for Toddlers

      The deer — tall, gentle and gone before you can point. Most toddlers meet deer at a safari park or in the forest's early morning, and the card brings that quiet bigness home.

      Teaching tips

      What this card plants

      Brings the biggest quiet neighbour into reach for children who live far from woods.

      Meet one for real

      Early evenings in a country park are your best chance — whisper.

      What kids learn from it

      Practises soft footsteps and hushed voices — big ears are listening.

      How to print it

      A5 or bigger — this one deserves a poster spot.

      Grown-up tip

      A real sighting is family legend material — retell it often.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Deer lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · GARDEN FRIENDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Snake Flashcard for Toddlers

      The garden snake, lying in the warm sun like a ribbon. It is the quietest neighbour in the set — no bark, no song, just a slow slither and a very important rule.

      Teaching tips

      What this card plants

      Handles the reptile question early, calmly and without the squeaking.

      Meet one for real

      On warm paths, keep eyes on the verge — most snakes slink off first.

      What kids learn from it

      Develops level-headed respect — no panic, no touching, just distance.

      How to print it

      Pin it calmly by the garden door at reading height.

      Grown-up tip

      The rule is boring on purpose — back away, fetch a grown-up.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Snake lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · GARDEN FRIENDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Bat Flashcard for Toddlers

      The bat — the night sky's acrobat, flying by sound. It comes out at dusk, flips and turns after insects, and sleeps upside down, a fact that delights every toddler who hears it.

      Teaching tips

      What this card plants

      Covers the one animal your toddler only ever meets as a flicker.

      Meet one for real

      Stand outside at dusk and follow the zigzag silhouettes overhead.

      What kids learn from it

      Links sound and flight — early listening science, no daylight needed.

      How to print it

      Laminate and keep by the door for after-tea walks.

      Grown-up tip

      Watch, don't chase — bats have somewhere to be.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Bat lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · GARDEN FRIENDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Owl Flashcard for Toddlers

      The owl — big silent wings, huge round eyes, and a hoot that belongs to bedtime. It watches the garden all night while everyone sleeps, which makes it the ideal last card of the day.

      Teaching tips

      What this card plants

      Adds the final neighbour to the list — wise eyes, soft wings, hoots at bedtime.

      Meet one for real

      Listen for hoots through the window on late summer evenings.

      What kids learn from it

      Opens night-day thinking — some neighbours keep opposite hours.

      How to print it

      Ribbon through a hole-punch — this one hangs on a door handle.

      Grown-up tip

      Save owl voices for evenings — a soft hoot is the game.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Owl lesson on the Learning Path.
